blindSourceSummaries: An international human-rights organisation news release (29 October 2025): a leaked draft omnibus reform (a proposed judicial package) would amend the penal code so that acting 'contrary to biological sex and general morality' - or its promotion - carries up to three years in prison (an amendment to a penal-code provision on 'indecent acts'), restrict gender-affirming healthcare to people 25 and over under onerous eligibility rules, and allow criminal charges against trans people and the professionals who treat them; justified as protecting 'the family' and 'public morals'. The organisation called it one of the most alarming rights rollbacks of the decade and urged withdrawal.

An LGBTI+ rights organisation (24 February 2026) presents its annual rights report for 2025 - a year defined by a major siege against LGBTI+ people. Findings: anti-LGBTI+ hostility became explicit state policy in 2025 - targeting of LGBTI+ people as 'deviant' or 'a threat' by the head of state and senior officials raised officials' motivation and third-party impunity; a new family-affairs ministry became the implementing ministry; one LGBTI+ rights organisation was closed; platforms and broadcasters were penalised or withdrew; artistic events were cancelled. The report documents six violations of the right to life (three hate-motivated killings; trans people most affected), 89 torture/ill-treatment violations (51 the previous year, largely during assemblies) and 313 liberty violations in 2025 (about 2.5 times the previous year, mostly detentions). No official hate-crime statistics exist; cases rely on media.

NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time (only site navigation was retrieved); the underlying article (31 July 2025) covers about 20 trans women in a major-city district rounded up for identity checks at a police station - names recorded, videos filmed, no official reason given - described as the 31 July 2025 mass ID roundups.
